hypothesis: interpreter-backed UB/effect evidence for EFFECT/STATE semantics

measurement.ub_surface: 0 unsafe blocks, 0 unsafe fns, 0 unsafe impls, 0 extern blocks in the 96 workspace Rust files (syn enumeration; the only textual hits are test-fixture string literals) -- safe Rust has no UB up to compiler/std soundness bugs, so Miri's core mechanism (Stacked/Tree Borrows, alignment, uninit, data-race detection on unsafe code) has no target here
measurement.availability: Miri is a nightly-only rustup component; the pinned toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml: 1.90.0, components rustfmt+clippy) cannot run it, so it is not even usable as an execution oracle without changing the pin
measurement.effect_surface: Miri's shims model OS effects at the foreign-function boundary (src/shims/unix/foreign_items.rs: open/read/write/stat/mkdir/rename/getenv/setenv/socket/bind/poll/clock_gettime/pthread_*, grouped fs, env, time, sync, socket, tls, alloc). Atlas's EFFECT dimension works at source level, where the boundary is the std API: 504 Atlas call sites reach effectful std modules (fs 352, process 63, env 50, io 20, time 17, thread 2; rust-analyzer SCIP at exact anchors) while EFFECT observes only INFERRED panic candidates
measurement.method: syn visitor over every workspace .rs file for unsafe constructs; rustup component availability for the pinned toolchain; SCIP join of CALL anchors to std descriptors

finding: the P0 EFFECT gap is real (504 effectful std calls unobserved) but its mechanism is resolving external std paths at the call site plus a std-path effect table -- an extension of G75's native resolver, not an interpreter and not a libc shim table
